recipes.name: Pineapple Casserole
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup white sugar, or to taste
40 buttery round crackers (such as Ritz®), crushed
0.5 cup butter, melted, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Drain the can of pineapple chunks, reserving 1/4 cup of the pineapple juice to use in this recipe. Discard remaining juice or reserve for a different use.
Transfer drained pineapple chunks and reserved 1/4 cup juice into a large bowl. Add drained, crushed pineapple, cheese, sugar, and flour; mix to combine.
Pour into a 1 ½-quart casserole dish.
Mix cracker crumbs and melted butter in a small bowl; sprinkle over pineapple mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pineapple Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This pineapple casserole with Cheddar cheese and a buttery cracker crust is a classic sweet and savory Southern recipe. It's easy, fruity, and delicious!

video.description: Believe it or not, pineapples and cheese are a match made in heaven. In this video, Roscoe makes a classic Southern picnic recipe for pineapple casserole using canned pineapple, cheddar cheese, and a buttery cracker crust. Each bite of this oven-baked side dish is packed with rich, cheesy flavor and the natural sweetness of everyone’s favorite tropical fruit!

review.reviewBody: Awesome dish!!!! This is an A plus & easy no fail recipe that I have been making for many years. It goes perfectly with ham & is my son's #1 request for family get-togethers no matter the occasion or menu. It can be make the day before (unbaked). I now use Panko crumbs on top for a real crunch & cut way down on the sugar to about 1/2 cup. Also, Splenda works well. Try it!!

As a born and bred Southerner I've enjoyed this authentic dish at every gathering of southerners I've ever attended from the time I was a very small child. Some variations I've seen included 1 cup of sweetened coconut, a can of drained Mandarin orange slices, chopped pecans, a small jar of maraschino cherries drained and cut in half, and a half bag of mini marshmallows. I've seen it served at everything from Sunday family dinners to dinner on the grounds at churches to family reunions to funerals and weddings to neighborhood potlucks and it is ALWAYS one of the first dishes to disappear. That many Southerners just can't be wrong. You should try this. This base recipe is the same at every occasion ENJOY!

Love this recipe have made it several times now for Easter Dinner! 1st time I made it I followed the recipe to a T but was good but overly sweet. I always Double the recipe and I use 3 20oz Cans Pineapple Tibits 1 20oz can Crushed Pineapple 1/2 cup reserved juice 4 cups Shredded Extra Sharp Cheddar shredded ( NOT Pre-Shredded) 3 TBS white sugar or skip altogether 1/2 cup flour 1/2 cup melted butter 2 Sleeves Ritz Crackers Bake in a 9x13 pan this way everyone gets some of the crackers which is a must!! Would have given 5 stars as written but it was too sweet for my taste.

I made this casserole yesterday. I used two cans of crushed pineapple and it was not dry like when you make it using the chucks. I also used shredded cheese and my cheese melted. I cooked the casserole for about fifteen minutes then added the cracker crumbs and cooked it another twenty minutes. It came out very moist and with just enough juice that it was not dry. Try making it this way and I think you will like it better. I did not cut back on any ingredients.

Put another layer of cheddar cheese & red hots (candy) sprinkled on top. Put under broiler for 30-60 seconds, or long enough to start melting the red hots. Sounds different, which it is, but you will be thrilled that you tried it. It's delicious!!! This is also great when put on a fried flour tortilla.

Excellent side for baked ham. For so few and such simple ingredients this is very good, and neither the flavor of the pineapple nor the sharp cheese is overwhelming. As someone said, don't knock it until you've tried it! I've now made versions of three pineapple casseroles and this is my favorite. I did tweak it very slightly; used tidbits in pineapple juice instead of the chunks, and used a combo of light brown and white sugars, 1/4 c. light brown sugar and about 2 Tbsp. white sugar. (Next time I might only use 1/3 c. light brown and call it good enough.) The pineapple is already pretty sweet and I often reduce a recipe's sugar just slightly. Also added a little sprinkle of salt. I grated my own sharp cheddar and used an 8-oz block, which might have been a little more than 2 cups shredded, unless compressed into the cup. I baked it in a 7 x 11" baking dish for 35 minutes until it was very fragrant, but that might only be my oven. When I make half a recipe I only use the can of tidbits and leave out the can of crushed, and still use the 1/4 c. of the reserved juice; and reduce other ingredients by half. (The crushed even when drained holds more juice than the tidbits or chunks do.) Thanks for sharing this recipe! 5 stars from me and might add to our Christmas menu next time.

The first time I made this I didn't have any Ritz crackers but had a big party size of pretzels, those crushed to powder almost became my topping. It was delicious and my 3 boys all loved it and so did I! We ate it all and every time I surprised them with it they would love it. Have moved closer to family and having Easter at my house so I'm making this as one of my sides. No one in this part of the family has had it yet so curious to see how they like it.

Holy nommers! Per suggestions, I cut the sugar to 1/2 cup and I used 1 stick of butter instead of a full cup and this was amazing. I also ran into issues with the cheese not melting. I may try grating my own cheese next time or using smaller shreds.
I've made this recipe for years, but with cornstarch instead of flour.
I am going to add some ham chunks to make a one dish meal!

I just put this together and I'll be cooking it in the morning. I replaced the white sugar with only 1/4 cup of raw sugar and added about 12 oz's of diced ham and a handful of roughly chopped pistachios. Before I cook it I'll top it with 1/2 panko and 1/2 saltines instead of Ritz. But overall this recipe sounds like a good foundation for me.

Very good. Very sweet. I would maybe add a little less sugar next time. Also, for this to be a standalone meal, it probably needs more heft to it such as some pasta or something. But very good and I would have had no idea these ingredients work so well together.
As a lifelong NorCal girl, I understand how odd this recipe may seem but I can tell you I’ve been making it for over 30 years whenever I cook ribs. It’s a fabulous complimentary dish!

I liked the overall flavors - but was expecting the cheese to melt and become more so the entire dish would be more Homogenous. Is the cheese supposed to remain separated out from the pineapple - or did I not bake it long enough? Would it work better to melt the cheese with the pineapple juice in a sauce pot till melted and THEN add it to the pineapple in the baking dish before adding the Ritz Cracker topping? While it was definitely tasty regardless, I didn’t think the end presentation was all that appealing. Am I the only one who thinks this?
So easy to make and delicious!

Made this for a church potluck, it was a huge success and first thing to disappear. I am a Georgia transplant and have lived here for many years and had never heard of this casserole, but all the locals definitely knew it and loved it. Very easy to make. Made exactly as written as I had never had it before. Will definitely be making again. Everyone said this is a must have with ham, so definitely looking forward to the next holiday to try them together.
Absolutely yummy! Thank you for sharing the recipe. Will make again for sure!!

I have to agree with the reviewer that was like “this is ok”. It tasted good and I really appreciate the recipe. If definitely encourage anyone to try it. It’s nice. It just didn’t pop the way I was hoping. I might try it again with less flour and maybe a sprinkle of cayenne. It was nice tho - thank you!
Absolutely delicious! ❤️
Wonderful flavors. My wife loved it. Really simple quick recipe. Will make again soon.
